The web design questions people ask most

These are the web design questions small business owners ask before they hire anyone: what it costs, how long it takes, who owns what, and whether any of it brings in customers. The six most common are answered at the bottom of this page. The rest are grouped below by topic.

Some answers point to other pages that go deeper. Where a fact comes from somewhere other than us, the source is listed at the end.

Web design and web development: what is the difference?

People use the two terms as if they meant the same thing, and on a small business site they mostly overlap. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics covers them in one occupational profile but splits the work in two.

Web design

The part a visitor experiences: page layout, navigation, and how easily someone can find what they came for. A designer's question is "can a customer on a phone find the phone number in two seconds?"

Web development

The part underneath: building and maintaining the site in code, and technical matters like how fast it loads and how much traffic it can take. A developer's question is "will this page load on one bar of signal?"

A large company might hire separate people for each. A local business does not need to. Maurice Johnson does the design, the writing and the build, which is one reason the site comes out consistent from page to page.

Cost and payment

How much does a website cost here?

Three one-time prices: Starter $497, Pro $997, Agency $1,997. The pricing page compares them line by line. For what websites cost across the industry, read how much a small business website costs.

What is monthly?

Only the optional AI agents and hosting. The AI chat widget on Pro is free for 14 days, then $297 a month. The AI phone agent on Agency is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep an agent, or $49 a month without one.

Is there a contract or a deposit?

No deposit and no contract. You see the free demo first and pay only if you choose a package. Payment goes through Stripe checkout.

Timelines and what you need to provide

How long until my site is live?

Starter goes live in 7 to 14 days. Agency pages arrive in waves, the first live inside two weeks. Pro's timeline is agreed when you order. The full walk-through is on how it works.

What slows it down?

Almost always, waiting on photos, service details or access to the domain.

What do I need to send?

Your business details, services, towns served, any photos and where your domain is registered. The client intake form collects these in one go.

I do not have good photos. Is that a problem?

No. You will be told exactly what to shoot with your phone. Real photos of your own work beat stock pictures.

Search, Google and getting found

Is SEO included?

The basics are in every package: page titles, descriptions and a sitemap submitted to Google. Pro adds schema markup and Google Business Profile setup. Agency adds keyword research across your service area. More on SEO web design.

Why does my site need to work well on a phone?

Because Google now crawls and indexes sites primarily as a phone sees them. Google announced in October 2023 that its move to mobile-first indexing was complete. Every site here is designed for the phone first.

What are city pages, and do I need them?

A city page is one page about one service, written for one town. Whether you need ten or fifty depends on how many towns you serve and how many different ways customers describe your work. How city pages work explains the math.

Ownership, domains and leaving

Who owns the website?

You do, outright, once it is paid for.

Who owns the domain name?

You should. ICANN calls the person or company that holds the rights to a domain the registrant. If a web designer registers your domain with their own details, they may be listed as the registrant instead of you, which is how owners get stuck. You can check yours with ICANN's free lookup tool.

What if I want to leave later?

The site is yours. The monthly add-ons are optional (the AI phone agent can be cancelled any time), and the one-time build does not lock you into anything.

Working with Dominion Web Design Pro

Where are you located?

Big Sandy, in East Texas. Sites are built and delivered remotely for businesses anywhere in the country, and there is no office anywhere else. More on the about page.

Do you use templates?

No page is filled into a template. Every page is written by hand for your business and the towns it serves.

Do you have reviews or a portfolio I can see?

Not on this site. Instead of asking you to trust a gallery, the free demo shows you a site built for your own business, which tells you more than someone else's would.

Common questions

What is the difference between web design and web development?

Web design is how the site looks and works for a visitor: the layout, the navigation, how easy it is to use. Web development is the technical build underneath: the code, how fast pages load and how much traffic the site can handle. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics splits the work along similar lines: designers handle layout, navigation and usability, developers handle the site's construction. A small business site needs both, and here one person, Maurice Johnson, handles both.

Who designs websites for small businesses?

Usually one of three: a freelancer working alone, a web design agency with a team, or the owner using a do-it-yourself builder. Dominion Web Design Pro is a small operation where the person who writes and builds your site, Maurice Johnson, is the one you deal with throughout.

What is a web design company, and what does it do?

A business that plans, writes, designs and builds websites for other businesses. A good one also sets up the search basics (page titles, descriptions, a sitemap and schema), connects your contact form and domain, and hands you a site you own.

Do I own my website and domain when it is finished?

You own the finished website outright once it is paid for. For the domain, make sure you are the registrant, the name on the registration record. ICANN notes that if a developer registers a domain with their own details, they can end up listed as the registrant instead of you. If you already own a domain, building the site does not change who it is registered to.

Can you promise my website will rank first on Google?

No, and nobody honestly can. Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. What we control is how the site is built: pages written for real searches, the search basics in place, and pages for the towns you serve.

Who answers the phone when I call?

An AI receptionist answers (903) 636-7511 any hour. Ask about a website preview, or ask for Maurice or a person, and it transfers you to Maurice.

Still have a question? The demo answers most of them.

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
